page: Amazon Web Services c5a.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual server running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. Hardware allocation includes 8 dedicated virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores, with two hardware threads per core. Memory provision consists of 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, though it omits AVX-512 and AMX extensions.

The instance does not feature bundled local storage, requiring the use of external network-attached volumes for all filesystem operations. It also contains no GPU accelerators. In terms of network connectivity, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard virtual network configuration for inbound and outbound routing.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across standard computational suites. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1345.0 and a multi-core score of 5187.0, alongside 7380.0 in Clang software compilation. PassMark testing yielded a CPU score of 10497.89 and a memory score of 2326.01. Operational throughput tests registered 7.49 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 7.73 GB/sec in static web serving. However, raw stress tests highlight performance tradeoffs: stress-ng CPU execution registered in lower percentiles, and uncached large-block memory bandwidth declined to 35.43 GB/sec for reads and 22.68 GB/sec for writes.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU distribution establishes the c5a.2xlarge as an efficient compute option for processing workloads that require stable multi-core processing without extensive memory footprints. Typical deployment environments include software compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, batch processing, distributed caching tiers, and lightweight machine learning inference, where small 135M parameter models achieve prompt processing speeds of 455.44 tokens per second.
description: Amazon Web Services c5a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz. The instance delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 16 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, resulting in a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps and operates without integrated local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating external network-attached storage. In benchmark evaluations, the c5a.2xlarge demonstrates middle-tier performance across general compute suites, scoring 10,497.89 in PassMark CPU tests and achieving 5,187 in Geekbench multi-core. However, raw stress-ng CPU execution and uncached memory bandwidth show comparatively lower performance percentiles. The hardware profile provides efficient compute capacity for standard compute-bound workloads, making it well matched for static web serving, Clang software compilation, Redis key-value workloads, and small-scale language model inference.
